text:
maria: morning team — new hire Jun here, hitting a networking blocker on day 1. Browser on Windows can reach our internal wiki and services, but tools inside WSL2 can't hit 10.10.0.0/16. Chrome → OK, `curl` in WSL → timeout. Anyone recognize this? :wave:

it-sam: welcome Jun! :tada: Which VPN client/version did you install and did you use the company installer from the portal? Also paste `ip route` from WSL and `route print` from Windows.

jun-newhire: Installed "CorpVPN 2.3.1" from the portal. Quick outputs:
```
# inside WSL2
$ ip route
default via 172.31.80.1 dev eth0
10.10.0.0/16 via 172.31.64.1 dev eth0 proto static
```
Windows `route print` shows the 10.10 route set on the vEthernet adapter for WSL with gateway 172.31.64.1.

infra-ryan: Two common causes: 1) WSL2 uses a NAT network and occasionally the host doesn't NAT traffic to the VPN adapter, or 2) split DNS isn't resolving internal hostnames inside WSL. Can you `nslookup internal-api` from WSL?

jun-newhire: `nslookup internal-api` in WSL returns server 172.31.64.1 but NXDOMAIN. In Windows it's fine.

maria: probably split-dns: Windows has a DNS suffix pushed by the VPN, WSL inherits different resolver behavior. For a quick test, try `sudo bash -c "echo 'nameserver 172.31.64.1' > /etc/resolv.conf"` then retry curl. If that works, we can make it persistent.

jun-newhire: I did that and now `curl http://internal-api/health` returns 200. Nice. But after a minute it stops resolving again.

it-sam: That aligns with WSL overwriting resolv.conf from Windows network state. Two paths: 1) tell WSL not to auto-generate resolv.conf and add the VPN DNS permanently (`/etc/wsl.conf` with `[network] generateResolvConf = false`), or 2) run a user-space proxy like `sshuttle` to forward the 10.10/16 CIDR through the bastion.

infra-ryan: If you want the least invasive: I can spin up an ephemeral dev VM inside the VPC (dev-ephem-jun-01) and give you RDP/SSH for 48h. That avoids changing host routes and is useful while IT evaluates the policy.

jun-newhire: Prefer not to change host config on day 1. Can I try sshuttle? Never used it before.

maria: sshuttle is pretty simple: on Windows WSL, install `pip install sshuttle`, then `sshuttle -r corp\u0040bastion.internal 10.10.0.0/16 -x 0.0.0.0/0` — it will proxy the CIDR over SSH through the bastion. Works well for dev access.

jun-newhire: Ran sshuttle and looks good — services reachable and DNS stable. Thanks!

it-sam: I'll file an IT ticket to look at WSL DNS persistence and whether we should push a policy for the VPN to register split-dns into the WSL resolver. Ticket IT-4310 opened and assigned to netadmin, priority: medium.

deploy-bot: Ticket/created 20IT-431020"WSL split-DNS & split-route for new hire" assigned to netadmin, link: https://issues.corp/IT-4310

jun-newhire: Thank you all — SSH tunnel + sshuttle and the ephemeral VM offer are both useful backups. Marking this resolved for now. :white_check_mark:
